newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares stagnant on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares stagnant on lack of demand.

text.p: Singapore shares were listless at weaker levels midday on Friday with a lack of arbitrage opportunities on over the counter stocks sapping activity, dealers said.
Institutional investors led selling on index-linked counters but many were likely to remain sidelined ahead of the weekend.
"The market is dead in the water. The only game in town are OTC Malaysian issues," a local brokerage dealer said, but added that volume in small cap stocks was also poor.
At the noon break, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was off 11.89 points at 2,008.28.
Volume was a meagre 49 million shares, with advancing issues at 154 against decliners at 114.
Dealers expect volume to continue thin ahead of further tests by the index of support at 2,000.

Keppel Corp shares continued their slide to a new low of S$6.50, down 30 cents. Volume was over 1.2 million shares. SPH foreign also eased 30 cents to S$26.80. The foreign tranches of local banks were also sold, weighed down by worries over exposure to Thailand's financial woes and a slowdown in mortgage loans in the domestic market. SIA foreign was the exception, rising 10 cents to S$12.40. -- Jacqueline Wong (65 8703080)
